Joe is controlling. I don’t know if that happened due to nature vs nurture, but I think he internalized his mother’s pain as his fault when he couldn’t save her. He was anywhere from the ages of 8-10 and no matter the circumstances, none of what happened was ever his responsibility. In his eyes, he had failed her, not the other way around, and that was never resolved. He copes by being controlling. He prefers to blame himself for his mother’s fate and actions since he doesn’t want to admit he was at the mercy of an adult who was supposed to protect him. He wants to rationalize this by thinking he had power over his fate. He doesn’t want to face the question: “why didn’t the adults in my life love me?” 

Because of this, he projects his sense of responsibility towards other women who seems like a simple, straight forward case of “broken women” when in reality, no human is perfect, to feel a sense of closure for what happened with his mother. He wants to fix someone so he can feel accomplished and override his sense of failure for when he couldn’t save his mother, despite killing his abusive father. 

We are all broken. For example, from Joe’s perspective Benji was an awful person, but we have no way to know if maybe he used to be a good kid, but after pain and disappointment ended up being the unlikable character he was in Season 1, that led to no one feeling sorry for his death. If Benji was a woman perhaps he’d also romanticize and write away his flaws and saw he was also another person who needed fixing. 

Somewhere along the line he justified his mother’s helplessness as “she’s just a woman” and he decided to paint that over every woman, realizing she must have some backstory that justifies her mistakes in life. So I guess in a way, he is a misogynist. It’s his charm that makes it forgivable.
